lead: An OSCE is a series of timed stations (about 5–8 min each) with a simulated patient, a model or data, marked on a fixed checklist. Every station has the same opening and closing, which carry easy marks.
f: History · examination on a model or patient · procedure (delivery, VE, BP, dipstick) · data (partogram, CTG) · drills (PPH, eclampsia, shoulder dystocia, cord prolapse, newborn) · spotters · counselling
Read the task twice: who, how many weeks, the verb (history, examine, counsel) · note what is given · run the checklist in your head: opening, task, closing

Hand hygiene · greet, introduce · confirm name and age · explain and consent · privacy and a female chaperone · closing: summarise, safety-net (bleeding, leaking, fewer movements), thank, cover, wash hands

sc: Male student about to examine a woman → Named female chaperone

f: ICE: ideas, concerns, expectations · open then closed questions · signposting · facts in 2–3 chunks · words she understands · teach-back

sc: Telling a mother her baby has died → SPIKES with a warning shot

f: BRAN: benefits, risks, alternatives, nothing (doing nothing) · capacity: understand, retain, weigh, communicate
Present in under 1 minute: who, why, positives, relevant negatives, impression, plan · one main differential · in any emergency viva the first words are "call for help"

tr: Never leave a medical word unexplained; let her speak first for about a minute
